scope: Ten reproducible real-data projects bundled with the Skill. Each project includes its reviewed source snapshot, source manifest, configuration, preparation and analysis code, Evidence Intelligence Report, all figures, machine-readable results, and an evidence-matched Decision Intelligence Brief.

cases.title: Heart-Failure Follow-up Risk and Survival
cases.question: How should censored follow-up evidence inform an illustrative triage-rule comparison without becoming a treatment claim?

source.version: UCI static archive snapshot; source file timestamp 2023-05-22

cases.result: Low ejection fraction is associated with higher observed risk; censoring-aware analysis supports external triage validation, not a treatment recommendation.
cases.terminal_output: Illustrative triage comparison requiring prospective or external validation
cases.boundary: Small observational cohort, incomplete treatment information, analyst-defined thresholds, and no causal treatment estimand.
cases.figure_alt: Multivariable Cox proportional-hazards estimates for the heart-failure cohort

cases.title: Pseudoword Reading: Repeated-Measures Inference
cases.question: How does passage type change eye-movement burden within the same participant, and how stable is the contrast across reader groups?

source.dataset: Eye movements of dyslexic and average readers in meaningful and pseudoword passage reading
source.grain: one de-identified participant with repeated passage measures

cases.result: Pseudoword passages increase fixation-duration burden; paired analysis preserves the repeated-measures design and exposes group heterogeneity.
cases.terminal_output: Bounded behavioral inference and future-study design target
cases.boundary: The public sample is small and does not establish downstream educational outcomes or an intervention effect.
cases.figure_alt: Participant-level paired passage contrast with bootstrap uncertainty

cases.title: End-to-End Census-Income Model Validation
cases.question: Does a benchmark classifier improve on simple baselines while remaining calibrated and acceptably stable across groups?

source.version: UCI static archive snapshot; files timestamped 2023-05-22
source.grain: one Census-derived person record meeting the dataset extraction rules

cases.result: The sparse logistic model improves on the baselines, but calibration and subgroup errors prevent consequential reuse.
cases.terminal_output: Validated benchmark with an explicit non-deployment boundary
cases.boundary: Historical 1994 data, missing categories, social-structure shift, and no validation for a real eligibility decision.
cases.figure_alt: Independent-test comparison of majority, naive Bayes, and sparse logistic models

cases.title: Bike-Demand Forecasting and Robust Allocation
cases.question: How should a fixed service resource be distributed across time blocks when demand is forecast out of time?

source.grain: one observed hour in the Capital Bikeshare system

headline_metrics.label: Forecast MAE improvement versus overall mean

cases.result: A robust time-block allocation reduces modeled unmet demand out of time, while the perfect-information bound limits the value of further forecast improvement.
cases.terminal_output: Bounded allocation recommendation with reversal conditions
cases.boundary: System totals omit station imbalance, routing, labor, service time, and causal effects; resource units are illustrative scalers.
cases.figure_alt: Held-out unmet demand across feasible bike-service allocation strategies

cases.title: Marketing Response and Capacity Planning
cases.question: Can pre-contact information concentrate observed responses under a fixed outreach capacity without using post-contact leakage?
cases.result: Pre-contact features weakly concentrate observed responses; common campaign shocks are preserved across capacity options.
cases.terminal_output: Exploratory capacity comparison requiring a randomized campaign
cases.boundary: Observed response concentration is not incremental lift, causal treatment effect, profit, or return on outreach.
cases.figure_alt: Held-out response capture across alternative marketing review capacities

cases.title: Treasury Yield-Curve Tail-Risk Engineering
cases.question: How do duration choices change historical tail loss, backtest behavior, and sensitivity to dependent market shocks?

source.dataset: Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates
source.grain: one U.S. Treasury business-day yield curve

methods: daily carry plus first-order duration response
cases.result: Longer-duration allocations show materially larger historical tail losses; the short allocation remains the risk reference.
cases.terminal_output: Risk-bounded duration comparison, not an investment instruction
cases.boundary: First-order duration omits convexity, security selection, costs, financing, taxes, liquidity, and future-regime uncertainty.
cases.figure_alt: Historical expected shortfall across illustrative Treasury duration allocations

cases.title: Regime-Aware Multi-Asset Portfolio Construction
cases.question: Can a transparent walk-forward allocation improve the historical risk-return trade-off without breaking turnover, tail-risk, or evidence constraints?

source.license: Yahoo terms of service; upstream market-data rights remain separate
source.grain: one common trading date across SPY, TLT, VNQ, GLD, and BIL

cases.result: The bounded adaptive rule reduced historical drawdown and tail loss relative to both benchmarks and had the highest return-to-volatility ratio, but it did not maximize sampled mean return.
cases.terminal_output: Prospective paper-portfolio validation; no investment instruction
cases.boundary: Provider terms apply; ETF histories omit future regimes, taxes, bid-ask spreads, impact, investor liabilities, capacity, and suitability.
cases.figure_alt: Walk-forward multi-asset portfolio growth beside equal-weight and 60/40 benchmarks

cases.title: Privacy-Preserving Complaint Monitoring and Negative Validation
cases.question: Does a privacy-minimized complaint model create reliable ranking gain over random review in a later calendar period?

source.dataset: Consumer Complaint Database: Money Transfer, Virtual Currency, or Money Service
source.version: Closed 2022 UTC window; privacy-minimized extract created 2026-07-27
source.grain: one 2022 complaint for a money-transfer, virtual-currency, or money-service product

cases.result: The model contains weak statistical signal but no reliable operational ranking gain at tested review capacities.
cases.boundary: The timely flag is not complaint merit, harm, resolution quality, company quality, or compliance; the 2022 model may not transport.
cases.figure_alt: Held-out cumulative gain curve compared with random complaint review

cases.title: Commercial Real Estate Transactions and Regeneration Risk
cases.question: Which borough/property-type segments have enough public transaction evidence for property-level diligence, and how do financing-rate assumptions change the income hurdle?

source.dataset: NYC Citywide Annualized Calendar Sales Update
source.publisher: New York City Department of Finance
source.license: NYC Open Data Terms of Use

cases.result: Public transactions support a market-depth screen and financing evidence request, not property valuation or acquisition.
cases.terminal_output: Property-level lease, condition, title, zoning, and financing diligence
cases.boundary: The source does not establish arm's-length status, NOI, expenses, occupancy, condition, appraisal value, debt terms, or causal regeneration effects.
cases.figure_alt: Commercial-property median transaction price per square foot across NYC boroughs

cases.title: Spatial Equity and Service-Hub Planning
cases.question: Where is need spatially clustered, and how do alternative hub strategies change modeled coverage under a fixed radius and capacity?

source.license: U.S. Government work / Census open data

cases.result: Need is spatially clustered, and a composite allocation balances poverty, transit dependence, and housing pressure better than a single-indicator rule.
cases.terminal_output: Planning-screen allocation with radius, weight, and geography reversal tests
cases.boundary: Straight-line centroid distance and tract aggregates are screening approximations; travel time, site feasibility, capacity, and ACS uncertainty require local review.
cases.figure_alt: Massachusetts tract-level need and selected service hubs
